title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a linear composite score (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than any single submetric. Using a synthetic NetOps Task Bank and a deterministic validator, we ran 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive artifacts (raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, and SHA‑256 hashes). Empirical result: every held‑out candidate validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined on this held‑out set because labels are constant (no outage positives). Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the full composite‑vs‑submetric AUC pipeline (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the preserved bundle. We (i) map principal claims to exact persisted artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 hash(es), (ii) give a deterministic reconstruction recipe restricted to preserved artifacts, and (iii) provide an exact artifact‑hygiene checklist (filenames and canonical fields) needed to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Agentic LLMs are increasingly used to propose executable NetOps changes (intent→configuration). Operational trust requires verifiable evidence that the surrounding safety machinery (validators, canary deployments, rollback trials, abort/abstain decisions) meaningfully predict runtime risk. Prior work emphasises generate–verify–repair pipelines and verifier orchestration as engineering foundations for operational NetOps (see cited works). Research question. CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 asked: "Can a composite canary–rollback score (linear combination of verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) predict emulator outage (binary) better than any single submetric?" Preregistration, artifacts, and boundaries. We froze a machine‑readable preregistration (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee) before any final execution. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) and adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Contributions. (1) a fully preregistered artifact archive and deterministic run; (2) an artifact‑grounded null/ceiling empirical outcome on the held‑out test (n11=200); (3) exact claim→artifact mappings (paths + SHA‑256) enabling independent verification of reported facts; (4) a deterministic reconstruction recipe and a precise artifact‑hygiene checklist to prevent the missing‑artifact failure seen here.
sections.related_work: Positioning. This study situates itself at the intersection of (i) verifier‑anchored generate–verify–repair architectures and (ii) verifier orchestration and cost‑aware verification policies. Representative verified sources used for comparative positioning (selected and verified per preregistration): MeshAgent (constraint‑guided NetOps adaptation) — https://doi.org/10.1145/3771567; GVR safety architectures for convergent correctness — https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6754899; SEVER sequential verification / Pandora/CUSUM policy — https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6810160; queueing/control for tool‑rich LLM serving — https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6438169; and an agentic NetOps survey used to motivate operational evaluation needs — https://openalex.org/W7161354925. We used these works for background and architectural framing only; experimental evidence and numerical claims below are artifact‑grounded in our preserved run.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistration JSON (SHA‑256 = 553509f5...) fixes: paired_binary design; synthetic task bank split deterministic by hash (train=300,val=100,test=200); planned_episode_count=400; shared_initial_generation semantics (one shared_initial candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded conditions); maximum_model_calls=400 (actual model_calls_used=200). The preregistration enumerated the composite feature vector: verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility and prescribed the analysis: train L2 logistic regression (5‑fold CV) on train+val to produce composite_model_weights.pkl, then evaluate AUC‑ROC/AUPRC on held‑out test and compare to best single submetric via DeLong; paired bootstrap (seed=1729,R=10000) for CI. Freeze evidence and artifacts. The run preserved raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace and normalized_configuration (execution/scoring/*.json), provider_call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the full execution manifest with per‑artifact SHA‑256 (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Key preserved artifact examples (exact path + SHA‑256): execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Submetric persistence policy (predeclared). The preregistration specified exact persisted objects required to compute the composite AUC pipeline: consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode fields: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility) and composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized feature_names, scaling_params, coefficients, intercept, training_rng_seed, CV spec). These two artifacts are required to deterministically reproduce the preregistered composite vs single‑submetric ROC comparison.
sections.results: Execution integrity. The execution manifest indicates planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the bundle). Per‑episode validator outcomes. For each paired task we persisted an execution/scoring/<episode>.json containing validator_trace.validation_after with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and a boolean valid field. Representative example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after.normalized_configuration and valid=true. Paired confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). The preserved paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) is: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4...) records baseline_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0 and guarded_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0. Confirmatory statistics (artifact‑reproducible). From the preserved contingency we reproduce: paired difference estimate = 0.0; paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0,0.0] with bootstrap_seed=1729 and R=10000; McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All values and the bootstrap invocation are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a...). Primary estimand status. The preregistered primary estimand — difference in AUC‑ROC (composite vs best single submetric) on held‑out test — is undefined on this preserved test because labels are constant (no outage positives); ROC/AUPRC require label variation. Missing persisted artifacts. The run did not persist consolidated_submetrics.csv nor composite_model_weights.pkl (both required by preregistration). Per‑submetric availability (artifact‑grounded): 1) verifier_coverage — PRESENT. Extraction path: execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and required_command_count (example: task-000001 baseline JSON). 2) canary_sim_pass — ABSENT (no canary simulator logs persisted). 3) rollback_success_prob — ABSENT (no rollback trial logs persisted). 4) LLM_confidence — ABSENT (provider_call traces lack numeric confidence field). 5) abstention_utility — ABSENT. Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑limited). Using preserved scoring JSONs and provider_call traces one can: (A) extract per‑episode validator boolean labels and verifier_coverage to reproduce the paired contingency and McNemar/bootstrap results (already done); (B) recompute ROC/AUPRC comparisons only if consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl are available or if canary/rollback/provider confidence fields are reconstructed and saved — they are not present. Representative preserved examples (paths + SHA‑256) that support the main empirical facts: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (90844c2b...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (8f38c8be...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (7bc1bd2a...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (1cb072b4...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (c56b737a...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational implications. The artifact‑backed null (ceiling) outcome shows that under the chosen synthetic task generator, model (gpt-5-mini), and deterministic validator, no emulator outages occurred on held‑out tasks. For the preregistered objective of demonstrating discriminative predictive power (AUC) of a composite score this is a degenerate outcome: ROC/AUPRC are undefined for constant labels. Scientific value of null/ceiling findings. Documenting and preserving a complete artifact trail for a null/ceiling result is important: it shows how task bank design, difficulty calibration, and persistence of runtime submetrics determine whether a confirmatory discriminative evaluation can succeed. Practical recommendations (artifact‑hygiene checklist — exact filenames and canonical fields). To enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations we require the following exact persisted files and fields at runtime: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv — CSV columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility. 2) composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized object with keys: feature_names (list), scaling_params (dict mean/scale), coefficients (array), intercept (float), training_rng_seed (int), cv_spec (dict). 3) canary_simulator_log.json — per‑episode keys: episode_id,canary_seed,canary_result_boolean,canary_trace_path,canary_trace_sha256. 4) rollback_trial_log.json — per‑episode keys: episode_id,rollback_seed,rollback_success_prob,rollback_trace_path,rollback_trace_sha256. 5) retrain_script.py + requirements.txt (pinned versions) and the training RNG seed. 6) preserve analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (already present). Rationale: these exact files allow deterministic retraining, reproducible inference of composite coefficients, and computation of AUC/AUPRC on held‑out labels. Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal: shared_initial generation semantics (one shared initial candidate per pair) reduces generation variance and may mask prompt sensitivity; the preregistration documented this choice. Construct: synthetic emulator labels may diverge from complex production outage semantics. External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and the synthetic task bank limit generality. Missingness: absent consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl block recomputation of the preregistered AUC pipeline. Reproducibility and deterministic checks. The deterministic_reconciliation.json (analysis artifact) documents pair accounting (complete_pair_count = 200), provider_call audit (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200), and that all deterministic consistency checks passed. The exact manifest and per‑artifact SHA‑256s enable bit‑level verification of the claims above.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered, executed, and archived a deterministic paired confirmatory study to evaluate a canary–rollback composite score for predicting emulator outages. The preserved artifacts (paths and SHA‑256s quoted above) support the concrete findings: completed episodes = 400; held‑out pairs = 200; baseline_success = 200; guarded_success = 200; paired difference = 0.0 with bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC primary estimand is undefined on the held‑out test because no outage positives occurred. Two preregistered objects required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) were not persisted; we document this omission and provide the exact artifact‑hygiene checklist and deterministic reconstruction recipe. The scientific contribution is an artifact‑grounded reproducibility report: it (i) maps claims to persisted artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes, (ii) demonstrates how ceiling outcomes can arise under deterministic synthetic task banks, and (iii) supplies precise operational recommendations and an exact file checklist to enable future non‑degenerate discriminative NetOps evaluations.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary. A human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Execution and artifacts. The run preserved raw model responses and per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json), provider_call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), an execution_manifest.json enumerating all artifacts and per‑artifact SHA‑256, and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Representative preserved artifact hashes used in the manuscript: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Missing persisted artifacts and effect on primary estimand. The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl to be persisted to enable deterministic retraining and computation of the preregistered composite AUC comparison; neither file is present in the preserved manifest. Consequently, the preregistered primary estimand (difference in AUC‑ROC: composite vs best single submetric) could not be computed on the preserved test set. Safety and scope. All experiments were run on synthetic tasks and containerized emulators; no production devices were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count = 0). The run preserved exhaustive logs and hash manifests to support independent artifact verification. Post‑lock human edits. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real‑world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single declared model: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator‑derived outage labels may not map one‑to‑one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl (required by preregistration) were not persisted, preventing recomputation of the preregistered composite discriminative analysis.
